title.es: Ser el entrenador de un amigo

es: Hacer de entrenador de un amigo: preguntar su objetivo, responder a sus excusas, aconsejar y acordar un plan.

teaching.en: A good coach asks first: what is your goal this month?
teaching.es: Un buen entrenador pregunta primero: ¿cuál es tu objetivo este mes?
teaching.explanationEs: El coach empieza por el objetivo de su amigo.
segments: A good coach asks first: what
teaching.audioText: A good coach asks first: what is your goal this month?

teaching.en: If a friend has an excuse, say: I understand, but try doing it for ten minutes.
teaching.es: Si un amigo pone una excusa, di: te entiendo, pero prueba a hacerlo diez minutos.
teaching.explanationEs: Primero reconoce la excusa; después propón con try + gerundio.
segments: If a friend has an excuse, say: I
understand, but try doing it for ten minutes.
teaching.audioText: If a friend has an excuse, say: I understand, but try doing it for ten minutes.

teaching.en: Try leaving your shoes by the door, and remember to set an alarm.
teaching.es: Prueba a dejar los zapatos junto a la puerta y acuérdate de poner una alarma.
teaching.explanationEs: Try + gerundio propone un experimento; remember to + verbo, una tarea.
segments: Try leaving your shoes by the door,
and remember to set an alarm.
teaching.audioText: Try leaving your shoes by the door, and remember to set an alarm.

teaching.en: As your coach, I say: stop checking your phone at night.
teaching.es: Como tu entrenador, te digo: deja de mirar el móvil por la noche.
teaching.explanationEs: Stop + gerundio pide dejar un hábito.
segments: As your coach, I say: stop
teaching.audioText: As your coach, I say: stop checking your phone at night.

teaching.en: We agree on a plan: I promise to call you on Friday, and you promise to try again.
teaching.es: Acordamos un plan: te prometo llamarte el viernes y tú prometes intentarlo de nuevo.
teaching.explanationEs: Promise + to + verbo: el compromiso de cada uno.
segments: We agree on a plan: I promise to call
you on Friday, and you promise to try again.
teaching.audioText: We agree on a plan: I promise to call you on Friday, and you promise to try again.

teaching.en: If you miss a day, do not stop. Just go on walking the next morning.
teaching.es: Si faltas un día, no pares. Sigue caminando a la mañana siguiente.
teaching.explanationEs: Miss a day: faltar un día. Go on + gerundio: seguir con el plan.
segments: If you miss a day, do not stop.
Just go on walking the next morning.
teaching.audioText: If you miss a day, do not stop. Just go on walking the next morning.

prompt.es: Tu amigo dice que está muy cansado. ¿Qué respuesta suena cortés y útil?

choices.text: I understand, but stop walking for ten minutes.
You are tired, so stop making excuses.
I understand, but try walking for ten minutes.

feedback.es: Primero se reconoce la excusa (I understand) y luego se propone un experimento pequeño con try + gerundio. Stop walking pide dejar de caminar, y «stop making excuses» regaña en lugar de ayudar.

hint.es: Reconoce la excusa y propón algo pequeño con try + gerundio.

feedback.es: Promise + to + verbo base expresa el compromiso: to call.

hint.es: Promise va seguido de to y un verbo.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase pide con claridad que tu amigo deje un mal hábito?

choices.text: You should stop checking your phone at night.
You should remember checking your phone at night.
You should stop to check your phone at night.

feedback.es: Should + stop + gerundio pide dejar el hábito. Stop to check significaría pararse para mirar el móvil, y remember checking sería recordar algo que ya hiciste.

hint.es: Tras should va el verbo base; el consejo es dejar el hábito, no pararse a hacerlo.

prompt.es: Ordena: «¿Por qué no pruebas a caminar después de comer?»

answer.text: Why don't you try walking after lunch

feedback.es: Why don't you + verbo base sugiere con cortesía; try + gerundio propone el experimento.

prompt.es: Escucha a la entrenadora y elige qué debe recordar Leo.

choices.text: Leave his bag at the gym.
Set his alarm before going to bed.
Stop using his alarm.

feedback.es: Remember to set es la tarea que debe recordar: poner la alarma. Dejar la bolsa junto a la puerta es solo un experimento.

origin.audio: Leo, remember to set an alarm tonight, and try leaving your bag by the door.

prompt.es: Completa: «Si faltas un día, sigue caminando al día siguiente.»

feedback.es: Go on + gerundio anima a continuar con lo que ya hacías: seguir caminando.

origin.text: If you miss a day, go on ___ the next day.

prompt.es: Responde a la excusa de tu amigo con un consejo y una promesa.

answer.text: I understand, but try going to bed earlier tonight, and remember to set an alarm. You should also stop using your phone in bed. Our plan is simple: I promise to call you on Friday, and you promise to try again. You can do it! Is that OK?
accepted: I understand, but try going to bed earlier tonight, and remember to set an alarm. You should also stop using your phone in bed. Our plan is simple: I promise to call you on Friday, and you promise to try again. You can do it! Is that OK?
I know you are tired, but try sleeping earlier tonight. You should stop checking your phone at night, and remember to set an alarm. I promise to call you on Friday, and we can make a plan together.

feedback.es: Una buena respuesta de entrenador reconoce la excusa, da dos consejos (try + gerundio y stop + gerundio o remember to) y cierra con un plan y una promesa: I promise to call you.

origin.text: Tu amigo Leo te escribe: «I want to run every morning, but I am always tired and I sleep late.» Responde con un mensaje: reconoce su excusa, dale dos consejos (uno con try + gerundio y otro con stop + gerundio o remember to) y acordad un plan con una promesa.

prompt.es: Escucha el audio y elige qué plan acuerdan los amigos.

choices.text: Tom will drink coffee only at night, and a friend will call him on Friday.
Tom will stop for a coffee at night, and he will call a friend on Friday.
Tom will not drink coffee at night, and a friend will call him on Friday.

feedback.es: Stop drinking es dejar de beber café por la noche, y la promesa es llamar a Tom el viernes.

origin.audio: Tom will stop drinking coffee at night, and I promise to call him on Friday.

prompt.es: Lee el mensaje. ¿Qué excusa pone Sara?

choices.text: She did not pack her bag.
She has no time.
She is too tired to swim.

feedback.es: Sara dice «I forgot to pack my bag»: la excusa es que olvidó preparar la bolsa.

origin.text: Sara: I wanted to swim this morning, but I forgot to pack my bag. I regret not doing it last night.

prompt.es: Completa: «Acuérdate de poner una alarma para mañana.»

feedback.es: Remember + to + verbo: la tarea acordada es poner la alarma.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase anima a un amigo a seguir con el plan?

choices.text: Stop walking; you are making progress.
Go on walking; you are making progress.
Try walking; you are making progress.

feedback.es: Go on + gerundio anima a continuar. Stop lo contradice y try walking propone probar algo, no seguir.

prompt.es: Escribe un consejo para un amigo que olvida beber agua.

answer.text: Remember to drink a glass of water every hour.
accepted: Remember to drink a glass of water every hour.
Try drinking a glass of water every hour.
Try drinking water every hour at work.

feedback.es: El consejo usa remember to + verbo para la tarea o try + gerundio para el experimento, con una frecuencia clara.

origin.text: Tu amigo olvida beber agua en el trabajo. Dale un consejo con remember to o con try + gerundio.

prompt.es: Escucha a Mia y elige qué lamenta.

choices.text: She will eat late today.
She cannot sleep early.
She ate late yesterday.

feedback.es: Regret eating lamenta algo que ya hizo: comer tan tarde anoche; hoy está cansada por eso.

origin.audio: Mia says: I regret eating so late last night, and today I am very tired.
